utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-08-91-T. The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we move into private session because as we have been alerted that there's something that Ms. Korner wishes to raise, could we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Matthew Olmsted, Joanna Korner, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Sorry I was notified that our Legal Assistant Dominic Kennedy is also in the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence this morning appearing, Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, Jason Antley, and Ms. Erin Dummavant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we, Ms. Korner, the matter that you wish to raise, should we be in private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we should.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning, to you, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You have not -- you will not at this stage be invited to make the solemn declaration to formally become a witness in this matter, but as a matter of courtesy to you, the Trial Chamber on its own behalf and on behalf of counsel on both sides, considering that you have been waiting to assist the Tribunal by testifying over several days, thought it should explain to you the reasons for the delay up to this point, and the further delay. As you may very well be aware, a trial is a process, and as such, it isn't -- it is seldom possible to anticipate the various factors, circumstances, and events which would not allow the process to go as smoothly as would have been anticipated. And it is for that reason that the -- that your being called to the stand has been delayed and I regret to advise will be further delayed, so that you will be -- you have an obligation, having come in as a potential witness, to remain at the call of the Court, of the Trial Chamber, until you are released. So although you have not yet been formally sworn as a witness, what is going to happen now is that you will be excused until the Prosecution, at whose instance you have been called as a witness, indicates that they are ready to begin your testimony. So we apologise and regret the inconvenience, because we are satisfied there would have been personal inconvenience for you having to travel to The Hague and just wait until the witness ahead of you has completed his testimony and the -- trust that you understand all of this. And as I said, you will now be excused and it will be indicated when you will return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I would add, in terms of the time that you anticipate that this could take, that the remainder of the day's sitting time will be devoted to completing the witness ahead of you, but also for the Prosecution to sort out how it goes forward in terms of your testimony. So they will certainly communicate to you in the course of today when it is likely that your testimony -- when they would be in a position to begin your testimony. But, as I said, from what has been communicated to us in the course of today, it is something by mid-morning there's something that should be communicated to you. So with that, sir, you are excused, and the usher will escort you from the courtroom. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, so I have no right to comment? I can just take under notice what you said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, if you have a question, I will attempt to answer it, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my arrival here was scheduled and cancelled several times. I was in Belgrade. When I came here, I was told I would begin on Tuesday. I've been here for six or seven days already. And I have been waiting for the call previously on several occasions. I wanted also to go back and testify by videolink because these six, seven days I spent here are not the only time that I spent here. On several earlier occasions I was awaiting the beginning of my testimony and focusing on it. If I endure any more hassle, I'll be getting more and more nervous and I will not be a good witness. I don't think I've been treated fairly in a humane way that respects my dignity. If I have to be here and spend seven to ten days waiting, I suppose I must live with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'm sure the Prosecution has heard what you would have said, and what you've said appears on the record. And we will see how matters proceed from here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just, before Mr. Mandic leaves, and tell Your Honours, Mr. Mandic arrived here on Saturday, and he was brought here early specifically because the Defence requested that they have a day to speak to him. That may be a matter I'll return to later. But I appreciate and we are very sorry and we echo what Your Honours have said that there has been this delay, but I think that's all we can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we now move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 26th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
